mcqs.question: Who won the Thomas Cup at the 2026 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals held at Forum Horsens, Denmark?
mcqs.explanation: China won the 2026 Thomas Cup and secured its 12th title. France was the runner-up, while India and Denmark won the bronze medals; South Korea won the Uber Cup, not the Thomas Cup.

mcqs.question: Who was appointed Chef de Mission of India for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow?
mcqs.explanation: Rohit Rajpal was appointed India’s Chef de Mission for the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Ravi Bengani was the Deputy Chef de Mission, while Vandana Rao and Rahul Swamy were team managers.

mcqs.question:
India was awarded the 2027 Asian Relays and the 2028 Asian Indoor Athletics Championships.

Statement A: The 2027 Asian Relays will be held at the Sector-7 Sports Complex in Chandigarh.
Statement B: The 2028 Asian Indoor Athletics Championships will be held at Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. The 2027 Asian Relays were assigned to the Sector-7 Sports Complex, Chandigarh, while the 2028 Asian Indoor Athletics Championships were assigned to Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar.

mcqs.question: With reference to the Asian Weightlifting Championships 2026 held in Gandhinagar, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: India won 10 medals, comprising 1 silver and 9 bronze medals.
China’s medal tally comprised 21 gold, 12 silver and 9 bronze medals.
Gyaneshwari Yadav won silver in the women’s 53 kg snatch.
China topped the medal table with 41 medals.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that China won 9 bronze medals. China’s 41-medal tally comprised 21 gold, 12 silver and 8 bronze medals; the other statements correctly describe India’s haul and Gyaneshwari Yadav’s silver.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): Gurindervir Singh set the 100 m national record with a time of 10.09 seconds at the 29th National Senior Athletics Federation Cup in Ranchi.
Reason (R): The record was broken twice in 48 hours.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is true: Gurindervir Singh clocked 10.09 seconds on 23 May 2026 at the Ranchi event. Reason R is false because the record was broken three times in 48 hours, progressing from Gurindervir Singh’s 10.17 seconds to Animesh Kujur’s 10.15 seconds and then 10.09 seconds.

mcqs.question: Whom did Sourabh Kothari defeat in the final to retain the IBSF World Billiards title?
mcqs.explanation: Sourabh Kothari defeated Pankaj Advani 1133–477 in the final and defended his 2025 title. Manoj Kothari is Sourabh Kothari’s father and an ex-world champion, while the other two options are associated with athletics.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the National Sports Board and Tribunal Rules, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The Rules were notified under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025.
2. The National Sports Board recognises National Sports Federations and consists of a Chairperson and two members.
3. The National Sports Tribunal provides for online filing and virtual hearings.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The Rules were notified under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025; the Board recognises National Sports Federations and has a Chairperson with two members; and the Tribunal permits online filing and virtual hearings.

mcqs.question: At which venue was Bharat Singh Chauhan re-elected as Chair of the Commonwealth Chess Association for the 2026–2030 term?
mcqs.explanation: Bharat Singh Chauhan was re-elected at the AGM held in Wadduwa, Sri Lanka, for the 2026–2030 term. Lausanne, Bonn and Kuwait City are associated with other sports organisations in the facts, not this AGM.

mcqs.question: Faustino Oro became the second-youngest Grandmaster in chess at approximately what age?
mcqs.explanation: Argentine prodigy Faustino Oro became a Grandmaster at approximately 12 years, 6 months and 26 days. The age of 12 years, 4 months and 25 days belongs to Abhimanyu Mishra, who remains the youngest Grandmaster.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements about the proposed transfer of para shooting governance:
1. Para Shooting is to move from the IPC to the ISSF.
2. The new system is scheduled to begin from 2027, with a transition during 2027–28.
3. The ISSF is headquartered in Munich and is headed by Luciano Rossi.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct: para shooting is proposed to move from the IPC to the ISSF, the new system is planned from 2027 with a 2027–28 transition, and the ISSF is based in Munich with Luciano Rossi as President. The agreement still requires approval at the 2026 General Assembly.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Everest summit records is incorrect?
options: Kami Rita Sherpa’s 32nd Everest summit is the men’s record.
Lhakpa Sherpa’s 10th Everest summit is the women’s record.
Everest is 8,849 metres high and lies on the Nepal–China border.
K2 is the second-highest mountain and lies on the Pakistan–China border.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement changes Lhakpa Sherpa’s record from the 11th summit to the 10th; her 11th summit is the women’s record. Kami Rita’s 32nd summit is the men’s record, while Everest and K2 have the stated heights and border locations.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: NADA imposed a seven-year ban on discus thrower Banveer Singh after extending his earlier five-year suspension by two years.
Statement B: Long-distance runner Harendra Kumar received an additional four-year ban.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true. Banveer Singh’s earlier five-year suspension was extended by two years to a seven-year ban, while Harendra Kumar received an additional four-year ban.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II in the context of the book on India’s first Olympic hockey gold.

List-I
 a. Author of “India's Olympic Gold: Hockey Triumph at Amsterdam”
 b. Dignitaries who unveiled the book
 c. Year and venue of India’s first Olympic hockey gold
 d. Publisher of the book

List-II
 i. Stick to Hockey
 ii. K. Arumugam
 iii. 1928 Amsterdam
 iv. P.T. Usha and Dilip Tirkey
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-ii, b-iv, c-iii and d-i: K. Arumugam authored the book, P.T. Usha and Dilip Tirkey unveiled it, India won its first Olympic hockey gold at Amsterdam in 1928, and Stick to Hockey published it. The other codes interchange the author, dignitaries, year and publisher.

mcqs.question:
With reference to the 2026 Thomas and Uber Cup Finals, consider the following statements:
1. Japan and Indonesia won the bronze medals in the Uber Cup.
2. Indonesia holds the record for the most Thomas Cup titles with 12 titles.
3. Both the Thomas Cup and the Uber Cup were established in 1949.
mcqs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Japan and Indonesia won the Uber Cup bronze medals. Statement 2 is incorrect because Indonesia has 14 Thomas Cup titles, while Statement 3 is incorrect because the Uber Cup was established in 1956–57.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The first Commonwealth Games were held at Hamilton, Canada, in 1934.
Statement B: The Commonwealth Games are held every 4 years.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is false because the first Commonwealth Games were held at Hamilton, Canada, in 1930. Statement B is true because the Games are held every 4 years.

mcqs.question: Who were the President and Chief Executive Officer, respectively, of the Indian Olympic Association in the context of the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
mcqs.explanation: P.T. Usha was the President of the Indian Olympic Association, while Raghuram Iyer was its Chief Executive Officer. The other options combine team managers, the Deputy Chef de Mission and the Chef de Mission.

mcqs.keyword: Asian athletics bodies and decision venue
mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the hosting of the Asian athletics events in India.

List-I
 a. Asian Athletics Association — establishment
 b. Asian Athletics Association — headquarters
 c. Athletics Federation of India — establishment
 d. Council meeting that decided the hosting

List-II
 i. 1973
 ii. Doha
 iii. 1946
 iv. Hong Kong

Select the correct code:
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv. The Asian Athletics Association was established in 1973 and is headquartered in Doha; the Athletics Federation of India was established in 1946, and the decision was taken at the council meeting in Hong Kong.

mcqs.question: The Asian U15 Boxing Championships in Tashkent were organised by which body, and what does U15 denote?
options: International Weightlifting Federation; athletes below 15 years
Asian Athletics Association; athletes below 15 years
Asian Boxing Confederation; athletes below 17 years
Asian Boxing Confederation; athletes below 15 years
mcqs.explanation: The championships were organised by the Asian Boxing Confederation, and U15 refers to athletes below 15 years. The other options alter either the organising body or the age category.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The Athletics Federation of India is the national governing body for athletics.
Reason (R): The Athletics Federation of India is the national governing body for weightlifting.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is true because the Athletics Federation of India is the national governing body for athletics. Reason R is false because the stated role of the Federation concerns athletics, not weightlifting.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the International Billiards and Snooker Federation (IBSF)?
options: Established in 1905 and headquartered in Lausanne
Established in 1971 and headquartered in Doha
Established in 1973 and headquartered in Doha
Established in 1946 and headquartered in New Delhi
mcqs.explanation: The IBSF was established in 1971 and is headquartered in Doha. The other options use the establishment years or locations associated with other sports bodies.

mcqs.question: Who was the Union Sports Minister associated with the National Sports Board and Tribunal Rules, 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Mansukh Mandaviya was the Sports Minister associated with the National Sports Board and Tribunal Rules, 2026. P.T. Usha and Raghuram Iyer held Indian Olympic Association positions, while Rohit Rajpal was the Chef de Mission.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Commonwealth Table Tennis Championships 2026 in Delhi.

List-I
 a. Edition
 b. Dates
 c. Venue
 d. Participating countries

List-II
 i. 22nd
 ii. 27 July – 2 August 2026
 iii. Thyagaraj Stadium, New Delhi
 iv. 35+ countries

Select the correct code:
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are a-i, b-ii, c-iii and d-iv. The championship was the 22nd edition, scheduled from 27 July to 2 August 2026 at Thyagaraj Stadium, New Delhi, with participation from 35+ countries.

mcqs.question: Which pairing is correct regarding the table tennis governing bodies mentioned in the context of the Commonwealth Table Tennis Championships 2026?
options: TTFI—established in 1946; ITTF—headquartered in New Delhi
TTFI—established in 1973; ITTF—headquartered in Hong Kong
mcqs.explanation: The Table Tennis Federation of India was established in 1926, while the International Table Tennis Federation is headquartered in Lausanne. The other pairings use details associated with different sports bodies or locations.

mcqs.question: The International Weightlifting Federation, associated with the Asian Weightlifting Championships 2026, has its headquarters in which city?
mcqs.explanation: The International Weightlifting Federation was established in 1905 and has its headquarters in Lausanne. Doha is associated with the headquarters of the Asian Athletics Association, while New Delhi is associated with the Athletics Federation of India.

mcqs.question: Who were elected as Vice-Chair, General Secretary and Treasurer, respectively, of the Commonwealth Chess Association for the 2026–2030 term?
options: Vicky Mago, Akhramshah Muammar Ubaidah and G. Lakshman Wijesuriya
G. Lakshman Wijesuriya, Vicky Mago and Akhramshah Muammar Ubaidah
Akhramshah Muammar Ubaidah, G. Lakshman Wijesuriya and Vicky Mago
Akhramshah Muammar Ubaidah, Vicky Mago and G. Lakshman Wijesuriya
mcqs.explanation: Akhramshah Muammar Ubaidah of Malaysia was elected Vice-Chair, G. Lakshman Wijesuriya of Sri Lanka became General Secretary, and Vicky Mago of South Africa became Treasurer. The tempting fourth option reverses the General Secretary and Treasurer positions.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding sports institutions:

1. The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961.
2. The Olympic Council of Asia was established in 1982, with its headquarters in Kuwait City.
3. The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1962.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961, and the Olympic Council of Asia was established in 1982 in Kuwait City. Statement 3 is incorrect because the correct year for instituting the Arjuna Award is 1961.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements are correct regarding the anti-doping cases and agencies?

1. Banveer Singh finished second at the Indian Grand Prix in Bhubaneswar in 2022.
2. NADA was established in 2005 in New Delhi under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
3. WADA was established in 1999 and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
4. NADA was established in 1999 and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is Only three. Statement 4 wrongly assigns WADA’s establishment year and headquarters to NADA; NADA was established in 2005 in New Delhi, whereas WADA was established in 1999 in Montreal.

mcqs.keyword: Sports personality and National Sports Day
mcqs.question: Major Dhyan Chand, associated with India’s first Olympic hockey gold, is popularly known by which title, and his birth anniversary is observed as what?
options: The Hockey Emperor; Khel Diwas on 26 January
The Flying Sikh; National Sports Day on 15 August
The Wall of Hockey; Olympic Day on 23 June
The Wizard of Hockey; National Sports Day on 29 August
mcqs.explanation: Major Dhyan Chand was known as the “Wizard of Hockey”, and his birth anniversary on 29 August is observed as National Sports Day. The other titles and dates do not match the stated association.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement A: Hockey India was established in 2009 and is headquartered in New Delhi.
Statement B: The Indian Olympic Association was established in 1982.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: Hockey India was established in 2009 in New Delhi. Statement B is false because the Indian Olympic Association was established in 1927, not 1982; 1982 is the establishment year of the Olympic Council of Asia.

mcqs.question: Which organisation governs Formula 1?
mcqs.explanation: Formula 1 is governed by the FIA, which was established in 1904 and is headquartered in Paris. The IOA, ISSF and IPC are different sports organisations and do not govern Formula 1.

mcqs.keyword: Indian Grand Prix venue and period
mcqs.question: The Indian Grand Prix was held at which circuit during 2011–2013?
mcqs.explanation: The Indian Grand Prix was held at Buddh International Circuit from 2011 to 2013. The other options refer to places or venues not identified as the Indian Grand Prix circuit.

mcqs.question: How many medals did India win at the Asian U15 Boxing Championships held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan?
mcqs.explanation: India won 27 medals at the Asian U15 Boxing Championships: 9 gold, 6 silver and 12 bronze. The figures 14 and 13 refer to the medal tallies of the U15 girls’ and boys’ teams respectively, while 9 is only the number of gold medals won by India.
